M1 — 2026-09-22
Branch bindings are unreliable when several sessions share one checkout, and the damage shows up a day later as a torn session. sofar_end_session rehomes the branch binding to the ending session's initiative, so with N sessions on `main` it is last-writer-wins: on 2026-09-22 three sessions moved `main` in two hours (r1-fixes, then rust-core, then memory-lead). Two consequences. (1) A session's OPENING events — session_started and the first command_runs — land in whatever the binding said at start, then re-homing moves the rest, leaving orphans behind: session 063dc84a has 3 events in drive-visibility and 211 in memory-lead, and `sofar doctor` reports FAIL — session spans 2 initiatives (torn, live). Fix it by appending a session_ended for that id to the record holding the orphans; it is an append recording a true fact, never a rewrite, and it is the hygiene of the record that HOLDS the strays, not of the initiative that owns the session. (2) Avoid causing it: pass `--initiative` (or the tool's `initiative`) explicitly on every write, and do the write-back with `sofar event append` from a per-initiative git worktree rather than from the shared checkout, which is the only mitigation that kept the binding still.
